narrative:
The model estimated an 88.3% probability that you will fail the bar exam on your first attempt, meaning failure was judged much more likely than passing. Because your law school application was tied to that prediction, it was rejected. Your gender and race were not used in this decision.

The denial was driven mainly by your class standing in the third year, which was the strongest factor. You are in decile 1, while accepted students averaged about decile 5.79; this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second strongest factor was your first-year class standing: you are also in decile 1, compared with an accepted average near decile 6, again pushing toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most important factor and it leaned toward passing, but at 2.90 it was below the accepted average of 3.23 and was not enough to offset the class-standing signals.

To improve future chances, ask admissions whether updated grades, a higher LSAT score, or additional academic work could be considered. Consider delaying application while strengthening your academic record, retaking the LSAT if appropriate, and applying to programs that review candidates holistically.
